Order 
This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the appellant/claimant seeking enhancement of compensation by taking exception to the impugned award dated 21.07.2010 passed by Third Additional MACT to the Court of First Additional MACT, Gwalior in Claim Case No.164/2009 whereby Claims Tribunal has exonerated Insurance Company from its liability to pay compensation.

entities.text: Court of First Additional MACT, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of death of Balkishan due to motor accident, Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.2,03,875/- with interest.
3.
Counsel for appellant submitted that compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal by assessing the income of deceased Rs.2,500/- per month is inadequate and on lower side.

It is further submitted that at the time of accident, deceased was working as vegetable vendor from which, he used to earn Rs.4,500/- per month and, therefore, prayed for assessing the income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act for unskilled labour.
It is further contended that Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24834 2 MA-1857-2010 Tribunal has also committed an error in not adding any future prospects in favour of appellant.

The further contention of appellant that Claims Tribunal has also erred in not awarding reasonable amount in other heads i.e. loss of estate,
loss of consortium, funeral expenses etc.
Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned award by enhancing appropriate compensation amount.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company by supporting the impugned award contended that Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount by exonerating Insurance Company from liability to pay compensation.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of appeal.

5. Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
After hearing counsel for the parties and on perusal of record, it is found that income of the deceased assessed by Claims Tribunal is on lower side.

In considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.3,195/- per month of an unskilled labour instead of Rs.2,500/- per month which has wrongly been assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

7. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimant is entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 25% and as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 13 has rightly been applied by the Claims Tribunal.

8. So far as the question regarding liability of the Insurance Company to pay compensation amount is concerned, it is not in dispute that at the time of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24834 3 MA-1857-2010 accident, owner of the offending vehicle was not having any valid fitness certificate which is clearly breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy and deceased was a third party.

Therefore, in light of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8 wherein it has been held that the Insurance Company shall be liable to make payment of the compensation amount with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver, therefore, the finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal with regard to totally exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability,
is not correct in the eyes of law.

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8

sentences.text: So, finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is hereby set aside and appeal is partly allowed to the extent that the Insurance Company shall firstly pay the compensation to the claimant with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the alleged vehicle.

Accordingly, appellant-claimant is entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-

 Loss of Income Rs.3,11,512/-

 Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
 Medical Expenses Rs.1,835/-

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,79,472/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24834 4 MA-1857-2010 Tribunal.
10.
In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.1,79,472/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal.
It is made clear that appellant/claimant is entitled to get interest from 05.08.2014 till passing of this order.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

11. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellant-claimant within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
12. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellant/claimant stands disposed of.
